config.title: Configuration
config.subtitle: Manage system settings
config.page_subtitle: Changes apply immediately — the config manager notifies every subsystem on save.
config.protect_deletes: Hold deletions back instead of carrying them across
config.failover_readonly: Drop to read-only when the server is unreachable
config.certificate_name_hint: The name the web certificate is issued to — usually the DNS record the bridge is reached by. Leave empty to use the appliance hostname. Saving reissues a self-signed certificate for this name, after which the browser warns once. An uploaded CA-signed certificate is left untouched.
config.dhcp_machine_only_title: Applies to the machine side only
config.dhcp_machine_only_body: This DHCP server is bound exclusively to the TNC interface and never answers on the LAN. It hands addresses to the CNC machines behind the bridge.
config.smb_credentials_note: Default service account for every share. A share can override it in its own settings.
config.lan_side_hint: Faces the corporate network and the modern SMB server.
config.machine_side_hint: Faces the CNC machines. This bridge is their gateway.
config.apply_lan_hint: Saving applies the TNC side immediately — this browser is not on it. The LAN side is applied separately, with a rollback in case it cuts your connection.
config.machine_applied: Saved. The machine side is now live.
config.lan_applied: The LAN settings are live. Your connection was not affected.
config.lan_pending: Applied. Reconnect at {url}, sign in again and confirm — otherwise the previous settings come back automatically.
config.lan_pending_dhcp: Applied. The new address comes from DHCP; find it on your router, sign in again and confirm — otherwise the previous settings come back automatically.
config.cert_reissued: The certificate was reissued for the new hostname. Your browser will warn once about an unknown certificate — that is expected.
config.cert_kept_custom: The installed certificate came from a certificate authority and was left untouched. It still names the old hostname; a new one has to be uploaded by hand.
config.cert_reissue_failed: The certificate could not be reissued and still names the old hostname. The log has the details; it can be regenerated by hand under Security.
config.lan_confirmed: Confirmed. The new LAN settings are permanent.
config.pending_title: A network change is waiting for confirmation
config.pending_body: If you do not confirm within {time}, the previous settings are restored automatically. Confirm only once you are sure you can still reach this bridge.
config.pending_expired: The window has passed. The previous settings should be back; reload this page on the old address.
config.confirm_error: The change could not be confirmed.
config.lan_hostname_hint: The appliance's own name. Sent as its DHCP client name and used in its certificate. Leave empty to keep the current one.
config.machine_hostname_hint: The name the CNC machines connect to. Independent of the hostname above, because the machines are often configured with a name that cannot be changed.
config.apply_machine_hint: Changes to the machine side take effect immediately. Your connection is on the LAN side and is not affected.
config.machine_smb_title: SMB settings for the machine side
config.machine_smb_hint: These apply to the whole machine side, not to a single share — Samba reads one value per server. Per-share access is set on the share itself.
config.workgroup_hint: The workgroup the machines expect. WORKGROUP unless your controls were configured otherwise.
config.dos_charset_hint: Character set for SMB 1 clients. CP850 for German umlauts on HEIDENHAIN controls.
config.drift_title: Saved, but not active on the interface
config.drift_body: Configured: {configured}. Actually on the interface: {actual}. The last attempt to apply this failed. Press "Save and apply" to try again.
config.network_subtitle: How this appliance is cabled, and what each side does.
config.mode_subtitle: Pick what is on the machine side. It decides which settings below apply.
config.interfaces_subtitle: Addressing for each side of the bridge.
config.dhcp_subtitle: There is no other DHCP server on the machine segment, so the control gets its address from here — or you turn this off and set the address on the control by hand. The default range is one address wide.
config.internet_subtitle: Whether a control may route beyond the LAN through this bridge.
config.internet_access: Allow machines to reach the internet through the bridge
config.internet_access_hint: Off by default, and it should normally stay off: a CNC control runs an operating system that no longer receives security fixes. Turned on, the bridge routes the machine segment out through the LAN interface and masquerades behind its address — outward only, so nothing on the LAN can open a connection towards the control. Turn it on only for a specific need, such as a licence check or a vendor update server.
config.allow_beta_hint: Off means only releases declared stable are offered.
config.protect_deletes_hint: Off means the bridge behaves like the server share mounted directly: a program deleted on either side is deleted on both. The removed copy is kept in Versions either way.
config.mode_existing-network_body: There is already a machine network, with one or more controls on it and something handing out addresses. The bridge joins it and serves its share the way a file server would. The usual choice.
config.mode_single-machine_body: No machine network: one control is cabled straight to the bridge, which is that whole segment. The bridge hands out the address itself, and decides whether the control can reach anything beyond it.

locks.title: Locks & Conflicts
locks.subtitle: Manage file locks across machines and resolve any conflicts.
locks.conflict_restore_success: Restored version {restoredTo}. The content it replaced was saved as version {preRestoreVersionId}.

logs.title: Logs
logs.subtitle: System and sync logs
logs.no_log_description: Nothing matches the current filters yet.

versions.title: Versions
versions.subtitle: Every version captured before content was overwritten, and the ability to put any of it back.
versions.find_file_subtitle: Leave the path empty to see the whole share's history
versions.retention_note: Pinned versions and versions referenced by a conflict are never pruned, and the newest version of a file is always kept.
versions.no_versions_description: Versions appear here once the bridge has captured content that was about to be overwritten.
versions.restore_disabled_title: This is the file as it stands now
versions.restore_success: Restored {restoredTo}. The content it replaced was saved as version {preRestoreVersionId}, so this can be undone.
versions.restore_dialog_message: This writes the content of {path} as it was on {date} back into the share.
versions.restore_dialog_note: The file's current content is saved as a new version first, so this restore can itself be undone. If the file is open on a machine, the restore waits for the lock to clear.

updates.title: System Updates
updates.subtitle: Check for updates, review changelogs, and manage automatic update scheduling.
updates.current_beta_hint: This release is published on GitHub as a pre-release and has not been declared stable.
updates.current_channel_unknown: Whether this release is a pre-release is known only after an update check.
updates.schedule_note: Automatic updates can be scheduled to run at a specific time each week.
updates.up_to_date_body: Version {version} is the newest release. Checked {date}.
updates.load_failed: Could not load the update settings
updates.save_failed: Could not save the update settings
updates.os_updates_body: Installs Raspberry Pi OS package updates with apt. Package removals are never performed automatically.
updates.os_auto_reboot: Reboot when an update requires it
updates.os_auto_reboot_hint: Only reboots when an upgraded package actually asks for one. The bridge is unavailable for about two minutes.
updates.os_run_failed: Could not start the system update
updates.os_phase_cleaning: Removing packages that are no longer needed
updates.allow_beta_hint: Beta versions are published for testing before a release is declared stable. Applies to the scheduled check and to "Check for updates" alike.

files.title: File Browser
files.subtitle: Browse synchronized files and their version history
files.no_files_description: Try adjusting your filters or search query
files.select_file_description: Click a file to view details and version history
files.preview_truncated: Only the beginning of this file is shown. Download it to see the rest.
files.preview_not_text: This file is not text. Download it to open it in the right program.

auth.title: Login
auth.subtitle: Enter your credentials
auth.manage_bridge: Sign in to manage this bridge
auth.connection_error: Could not reach the bridge. Check the connection and try again.

errors.network_error: Network error. Please check your connection.
errors.server_error: Server error. Please try again later.

setup.subtitle: First-time setup
setup.password_intro: No administrator password has been set yet. Choose one now — until you do, anyone who can reach this bridge could set it.
setup.password_too_short: Password must be at least {min} characters
setup.passwords_differ: The two passwords do not match
setup.finish_intro: Your password is set and you are signed in as "admin".
setup.finish_next: Finishing closes the public setup endpoint for good. Network interfaces, the AD service account and shares are configured afterwards under Settings.
setup.connection_error: Could not reach the bridge. Check the connection and try again.

shares.title: Shares
shares.subtitle: Manage synchronized shares and per-share settings.
shares.none_description: Create your first share to begin synchronizing files.
shares.lan_side_hint: The share on the modern SMB server this bridge mirrors.
shares.machine_side: Machine side — what the controls see
shares.machine_side_hint: The SMB1 share the CNC machines mount from this bridge.
shares.smb_password_hint: Leave empty to use the global service account from Settings > SMB.
shares.smb_password_stored: A password is stored. Leave empty to keep it, or type a new one.
shares.share_name_hint: Letters, digits, underscore and hyphen. Decides the paths on this bridge.
shares.share_name_locked: Fixed after creation: it owns the mount point and the cache path.
shares.machine_guest_ok: Allow guest access from the machines
shares.machine_guest_ok_hint: Most TNC controls cannot authenticate. Turn this off only if yours can.
shares.create_subtitle: Define both ends: the server export, and the name the machines mount.
shares.create_error: The share could not be created.
shares.test_hint: Lists the share and connects to it. Nothing is written to the server.
shares.test_error: The test could not be run
shares.machine_user_hint: The account the machines log in with. Only used when guest access is off.
shares.machine_password_hint: The password the machines log in with.
shares.machine_password_stored: A password is stored. Leave empty to keep it.
shares.sync_settings_hint: Values that apply to the whole bridge. Everything that can differ between shares is in the share's own settings.
shares.sync_behaviour_hint: How conflicts are resolved and how much bandwidth syncing may use
shares.read_only_label: Read-only — pull from the server, never push back
shares.file_handling_hint: What is skipped, and how large a file may be
shares.exclude_patterns_hint: One glob per line. Matching files are never synced in either direction.
shares.max_file_size_hint: Larger files are skipped and reported rather than transferred
shares.advanced_hint: Rarely needed — the defaults suit almost every installation
shares.scan_interval_hint: How often the server side is checked for changes

security.certificate_subtitle: The TLS certificate this management interface is served with.
security.load_error: Could not read the current certificate.
security.install_error: The certificate could not be installed. Nothing was changed.
security.replaced_notice: Certificate replaced. Reload the page if your browser warns about it.
security.reconnect_warning: Replacing the certificate restarts the TLS session of this page. Your browser will reconnect, and with a self-signed certificate it will warn you again.
security.cert_none: No certificate is installed yet. Generate one below.
security.self_signed_hint: The hostname, every interface address and localhost are included automatically.
security.upload_hint: Paste a PEM certificate and its private key. Both are checked, and the running server has to accept them, before anything is stored.
security.chain_pem_hint: Optional. Needed when the issuing CA is not a root your clients trust.
security.download_hint: Install this certificate on your computer to stop the browser warning. The private key never leaves the appliance.
security.title: Security
security.subtitle: Sessions, sign-in protection and the certificate this interface is served with.

scheduling.custom_expression: This schedule was set up outside these fields ({cron}). Choosing below replaces it.
scheduling.day_of_month_hint: Up to the 28th, so the job also runs in February.
